doc.title: Walter Booker and Jimmy Cobb interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995

title: Playing with Joe Williams and his place in jazz singing
summary: Cobb recalls golf-tour gigs with Joe Williams and Keter Betts and seeing Williams at Club DeLisa. He says Williams brought blues to wider audiences and helped Basie's band.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Have either one of you had occasion to perform with Joe Williams?

Yeah. We had, occasionally we used to have a little thing where we’d go on a golf tour together. Joe, you know is a great lover of golf and so am I. And so we used to have a tour, I mean Keter Betts got into a thing where he would be like the musical director for this professional golfer that lives in Washington that was the pro at the golf course out there. So he got us all on the gig, and we used to go like, they did it for maybe 17 or 18 times, and we used to go play the music and play golf, because Keter is a golfer, Joe is a golfer. So we had to have occasions to play with Joe, you know and everybody else, supplying the rhythm section for everybody that needed it. So we used to do that. And right now I’m getting old and I can’t think, it was Lee Elder, he used to have a ProAm tournament like every year, and we used to go play music for it. Joe used to show up quite often on it. So I played with Joe. I haven’t played with him other than that. I remember Joe from a long time ago. I remember Joe when he was still in Chicago singing at a club named DeLisa. He was like the house singer in the Club DeLisa in the 40’s. So that’s what I know him from.
How do you feel like his sound typifies jazz vocals?

Oh well he did, you know he did a lot to bring a certain type of blues to certain people. You know because when he was with Count Basie’s band he matter-of-factly kind of saved Count Basie’s band for many. Because at that time the bands weren’t doing that well. So they got Joe and Joe was a real favorite singer, so he kind of helped the band. He helped them so much that I think Basie started to call him his son. So Joe kind of educated people to that music, you know, people that probably wasn’t listening to it before. Because you know he’s got a lot of clever things that you know, that he says in the blues, and he can really do the real funky blues too, and he can do the sophisticated blues. So I think lately they probably associate him with the latter, but he can do it all.
Absolutely. That’s probably what happened, yeah, he did raise up the, he did widen the listening audience’s ears to the blues form, and acceptance of it, you know what I mean?
And he kept Count Basie’s band working too.
You know people they can sit and listen to instrumentals for a while, but you know, every now and then say, when is somebody gonna be singing?
